about: Every attempt to land on the Moon from 2013 (Chang'e 3) to September 2026 that reached the landing phase. Outcomes are taken from NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera pages, which imaged every site. Causes are the ones the operator published. These are counts of what happened; they are never turned into a chance of success. Peregrine is not here: it was lost before it could attempt a landing.

records.name: HAKUTO-R Mission 1
records.cause: The lander's software rejected the altimeter's readings as faulty after it passed over a crater rim about 3 km high, underestimated its altitude and ran out of propellant before touchdown.

records.name: Luna 25
records.cause: An anomaly during a pre-landing manoeuvre sent the spacecraft into the rim of Pontecoulant G crater, about 400 km short of the intended landing point.

notes: Luna 25 was lost during descent preparations rather than in the final landing burn; it is counted because it was a landing mission that struck the Moon.

records.name: SLIM (Smart Lander for Investigating Moon)
records.cause: At about 50 m altitude, just before the obstacle-avoidance manoeuvre, one of the two main engines most likely lost its thrust. SLIM reached the surface about 55 m east of its target with its solar cells facing west, so it could not make power at first.

records.name: IM-1 (Odysseus)
records.cause: The lander's own laser rangefinders could not be used because their safety-enable switch was not changed before launch; NASA's Navigation Doppler Lidar payload was used for the descent instead. NASA describes Odysseus as 'gently leaning into the lunar surface'; LROC shows it on terrain sloped at about 12 degrees.

records.name: IM-2 (Athena)
records.cause: Athena hit the surface faster than intended and ended on its side in a 20 m crater. Intuitive Machines later named altimeter signal noise and distortion, and long shadows from the low Sun near the pole that confused its optical navigation.

records.cause: The laser rangefinder gave its first valid altitude below about 900 m instead of about 3 km, so the final braking came too late; ispace concluded the unit's performance had degraded in flight.
